description: Swap the nullish-coalescing operator for logical-or, so a falsy-but-defined value (0, '', false) that must survive is silently replaced by the fallback.

Widen a strict less-than bound to less-than-or-equal, introducing an off-by-one that admits one extra element/index. Requires spaces around the operator so TypeScript generics (Array<T>) and JSX tags are never candidates.

Widen a strict greater-than bound to greater-than-or-equal, introducing an off-by-one on the upper edge of a range check. Requires spaces around the operator so generics and JSX closing tags are never candidates.
Drop a leading `await`, turning an awaited promise into a fire-and-forget call whose result/rejection is silently discarded.

Neuter a single-line null/undefined guard (`if (x == null) return ...` / `if (!x) return ...`) by rewriting the condition to always-false, so the guard never fires. Block-form guards (`if (!x) {`) are not candidates: the replacement needs the return on the same line.
Swap logical AND for logical OR, flipping a conjunctive condition into a disjunctive one.
Invert a strict-equality check to strict-inequality, flipping the branch the condition takes.

Remove an auth-guard call (`.auth(...)`/`requireAuth(...)`) from the line, so the request proceeds unauthenticated. Only calls without nested parentheses are candidates, so the rewrite never leaves a dangling `)`.

Strip a `path.join(root, ...)` wrapper down to the raw joined argument, dropping the root prefix it provided (a first step toward traversal; a post-resolution containment check, if any, is a separate guard). Only calls without nested parentheses are candidates.

Swap the two bare-identifier arguments of a call, e.g. `combine(left, right)` -> `combine(right, left)`. A member-call receiver (`obj.combine(a, b)`) is fine, since the match only anchors on the identifier immediately before the opening paren. The replace re-anchors on the callee identifier, so an earlier bare pair on the same line (an arrow-function parameter list `(a, b) =>`) is left alone and the CALL is what gets swapped. Does NOT cover: nested calls (`f(g(a), b)`), string/numeric/other literals as an argument (`f("x", y)`), more than two arguments, spread arguments, or a comma without exactly one following space (this repo's prettier style).
